Sofia / Priyom — I updated the sheet with model footprints and two scenarios. Key callouts here (summary, full rows in the sheet):

- Baseline assumptions: 34B opt-like model requires ~60GB GPU memory at fp16 for a 32k working set with full KV cached per request. With int8 quantization we estimate ~38–42GB effective GPU resident; int4 (aggressive) drops further to ~28–32GB but requires extra CPU/GPU ops and may increase latency by ~10–20ms per token depending on kernel support.

- For steady 3 qps (avg) and 7 qps 95th spikes, a single A100-80GB node can handle ~1.6 concurrent 34B int8 sessions if we keep a per-request KV footprint and share cache across warm requests. With int4, optimistic concurrency rises to ~2.2 sessions.

- Recommended committed pool (initial):
  * Option A (conservative): 6x A100-80GB dedicated = supports 8–9 sustained clinical-assistant sessions with room for batch.
  * Option B (cost-optimized, int8): 4x A100-80GB + autoscale buffer = supports 10–12 sustained sessions assuming effective prefix caching and request coalescing.

- KV offload note: If MavenBio wants to pin per-request full KV in GPU memory for fastest tail latencies, commit to Option A. If willing to accept ~50–100ms variance on cold prefixes and use Redis-backed prefix cache with local prefetch, Option B + offload is viable and cheaper.

I'll call out the math rows we changed: memory per token/seq, KV ratio at 32k, and effective concurrency under batching windows.

—Marcus
Principal Infrastructure Engineer

Elena — a few practical tradeoffs to flag that often determine which option customers pick:

- Latency vs cost: int4 unlocks more density but may cause a small regression in generation quality and a modest per-token latency hit. For clinical summaries we typically recommend int8 for first 3 months of production, then consider int4 after evals.

- Headroom policy: For guaranteed SLA during your weekly morning spike window (9–11 PT), we propose a reserved headroom pool equal to 25% of committed capacity. That is typically implemented as a dedicated subset of GPUs that do not drain to batch.

- KV eviction/tiling: To reduce committed memory, we can tile KV storage by splitting 32k windows into 4x8k tiles and only materialize tiles actively touched by a session. This reduces steady memory but increases prefetch complexity. We'll include benchmarks in the final doc.

Action items: Elena — can you share a small set of production prompts (anonymized) and your quality bar for int4? That will let us run microbenchmarks to validate the 10–20ms/ token latency delta and the ROUGE-style quality impact.

—Priyom
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
